mutation_targets.rationale: removing F_AuthRequired lets the model invent a successful operation that was never authenticated, which is exactly the auth-bypass counterexample these assertions catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuthBypass { some op: Operation | op.succeeded = True and op.authenticated = False and op.kind = ListOp }

mutation_targets.rationale: removing the uniqueness constraint on TaskDeletion.task allows two log rows to reference the same task, simulating an UPDATE/DELETE on the append-only deletion log.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_DuplicateDeletionRow { some disj d1, d2: TaskDeletion | d1.task = d2.task }

mutation_targets.rationale: removing the completeness link allows a successful DeleteOp without a corresponding TaskDeletion row, which is the missing-audit-entry counterexample.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MissingDeletionLog { some op: Operation | op.kind = DeleteOp and op.succeeded = True and op.authenticated = True and no op.deletionRecord }

mutation_targets.rationale: removing the attribution constraint lets a deletion row record a different user than the operation's actual caller, the misattribution counterexample.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MisattributedDeletion { some op: Operation | op.kind = DeleteOp and op.succeeded = True and op.authenticated = True and some op.deletionRecord and op.deletionRecord.deletedBy != op.caller }

mutation_targets.rationale: removing the closed-task rule lets the model invent a successful PATCH on a Done task that doesn't simultaneously reopen it — the exact 409 task_closed scenario the contract is built to forbid.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_EditDoneWithoutReopen { some op: Operation | op.kind = EditOp and op.succeeded = True and op.authenticated = True and op.target.status = Done and op.setsStatusToOpen = False }

mutation_targets.rationale: removing the no-op-after-deletion rule allows a non-delete operation to target a task that has already been logged as deleted, breaking the 'deletion is permanent' guarantee.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OpAfterDeletion { some op: Operation, d: TaskDeletion | op.succeeded = True and op.kind = EditOp and op.target = d.task }
